meta.tagline: An AI workflow guide for privacy, authorship, and academic judgment
meta.note: Mode 3 scenarios are active for the August demo. All other mode scenarios are stubs — schema is correct, content is placeholder.

scenarios.title: Preparing a Briefing Memo
scenarios.shortDescription: Can I use AI to help draft a briefing memo from committee notes and draft policy language?
scenarios.fullDescription: A Faculty Affairs coordinator needs to prepare a briefing memo for an oversight committee. Available materials include recent committee meeting notes and a draft of revised policy language. Which materials can safely move into AI-assisted drafting?

steps.question: Do the committee notes contain personnel discussions, evaluation records, or references to individual faculty?

yes.label: Personnel Records & Confidential Files
yes.message: These committee notes are restricted. They contain personnel content and cannot enter any external AI tool. Extract and set aside before proceeding.

no.label: Policy Work in Progress
no.message: Procedural committee notes are safe for AI assistance. Review before including in any packet. Confirm no personnel references are present.

steps.question: Is this draft policy language in pre-approval status (not yet officially adopted)?

yes.label: Policy Work in Progress
yes.message: Draft policy language is safe for AI assistance with review. AI output cannot replace the official approval process.

no.label: Official Record & Approved Policy
no.message: This is approved policy — canonical record. Safe for AI reference and citation. Do not modify without completing the official approval process.

steps.description: Assemble packet from approved, non-restricted materials only. Restricted materials are excluded.
steps.packetInstructions: Include only materials routed to Layer 1 or Layer 2. Do not include Layer 5 materials.

steps.description: Generate a governance summary recording the routing decisions made, materials included, and review status.
steps.exportNote: This summary can be attached to a governance file or presented to an oversight committee as documentation of responsible AI use.

scenarios.demoNotes: Primary August demo scenario. Should run end-to-end without errors. All routing messages must be clear to a non-technical Faculty Affairs user.

scenarios.title: Routing Governance Documents for a Summary Report
scenarios.shortDescription: Which governance documents from a recent review cycle can I use in an AI-assisted summary?
scenarios.fullDescription: A department chair needs to prepare a summary report of a recent governance review cycle. Available materials include officially adopted policy, committee meeting notes, and draft revisions. Which documents can safely support AI-assisted synthesis?

steps.description: Sort materials into three categories: officially adopted policy, committee notes, and draft language before routing.

default.label: Official Record & Approved Policy
default.message: Approved policy is a canonical record. Safe for AI reference with attribution. Cite the source document when using AI to summarize or synthesize.

steps.question: Do the committee notes contain personnel discussions?

yes.label: Personnel Records & Confidential Files
yes.message: Restricted. Set aside entirely. Proceed with procedural notes only.

no.label: Policy Work in Progress
no.message: Procedural notes only — safe with review. Include in packet after confirming no personnel content.

default.label: Policy Work in Progress
default.message: Safe for AI assistance. Human review required before any language is used in official communications.

steps.description: Assemble packet from Layers 1 and 2 materials. Export governance summary documenting all routing decisions.

scenarios.demoNotes: Secondary August demo scenario. Use if the primary scenario needs a follow-on example or if the audience wants to see multi-document routing.
